Issued at 300 AM EST Sat Nov 21 2026

Today-Tonight...A weak surface low pressure continues to meander 
across the Florida peninsula this morning, with mid-level 
troughing assisting in lifting it northeastward through today. A 
pocket of deeper moisture (PWATs 1.7-1.8") will advect across the 
Florida peninsula as the low departs the area, increasing rain and
storm chances locally to 30-60%, highest across areas south of 
Orlando and Cape Canaveral. Southwest steering flow around 15-20 
mph will help keep activity moving across east central Florida, 
which should help reduce the chance for prolonged periods of 
rainfall across a single location. A Marginal Risk (1 out of 4) 
of excessive rainfall remains primarily focused across the coast
due to fully saturated soil conditions and flooded areas across 
east central Florida from previous days of rainfall. These areas 
will be prone to additional flooding if any moderate to heavy 
showers develop. Rainfall accumulations of 0.5-2" will be 
possible, and locally higher amounts cannot be ruled out. In 
addition to rainfall concerns, isolated storm development will be 
possible through the afternoon and early evening hours, primarily 
from Orlando to the Cape southward. Mid- level troughing drifting 
overhead will provide support aloft for development along with 
modest instability (MLCAPE 1000+ J/kg) and cool 500mb temperatures
(-10C to -9C). Any storms that do manage to develop will be 
capable of producing lightning strikes and wind gusts of 40-50 
mph. Additionally, the strongest storms have a low chance of 
producing small hail less than one inch. The highest coverage of 
activity is forecast to occur between 1 PM and 8 PM, with showers 
and storms pushing offshore into the evening and overnight hours.

Building cloud coverage is forecast through this morning and into
the afternoon hours as southwest winds around 10 mph advect 
moisture from the Gulf. Near to slightly above normal temperatures
are anticipated today as highs reach the upper 70s to low 80s 
this afternoon and lows only fall into the 60s tonight. At the 
beaches, a high risk of rip currents continues along the entire 
east central Florida coast due to lingering elevated seas and a 
long-period swell. Entering the ocean is not advised!

Sunday-Monday...The mid-level troughing continues to lift 
northeastward through the remainder of this weekend into the 
Carolinas, with quasi-zonal flow developing aloft behind it. At 
the surface, a weak boundary drifts southward across the Florida 
peninsula on Sunday as a low lifts northward towards the 
Carolinas. The boundary is anticipated to pass with little 
fanfare, though there does remain a chance for some isolated to 
scattered showers ahead of the boundary on Sunday across the 
Treasure Coast and Okeechobee County. Mostly dry elsewhere on 
Sunday and then areawide into Monday as high pressure builds 
across the area, with westerly winds around 10 mph on Sunday 
becoming more northerly around 5-10 mph on Monday. Temperatures 
are forecast to be near to slightly above normal Sunday and Monday
with highs in the mid 70s to low 80s and lows in the upper 50s to
low 60s.

At the beaches, a high risk of rip currents will continue through
at least Sunday, with current guidance indicating a return to a 
moderate risk of rip currents on Monday. Entering the ocean is not
advised through the remainder of this weekend!

Tuesday-Friday...The quasi-zonal flow aloft will weaken as 
shortwave energy approaches overhead on Tuesday ahead of a 
stronger trough/low digging southward across the southeastern US 
and across the northern Gulf towards mid-week. At the surface, 
broad low pressure develops across the Gulf along the 
aforementioned stalled boundary draped across south Florida, with 
troughing aloft helping to lift the surface low northeastward 
across the Florida peninsula mid week. This set-up will result in 
increasing moisture and rain chances across east central Florida 
starting across southern portions of the area on Tuesday and 
expanding to include the whole area into Wednesday as the low 
moves across the peninsula. There remains some discrepancies in 
timing between the global models, so will continue to closely 
monitor trends. Isolated storm development cannot be ruled out, 
though confidence in this remains low at this time. Behind the 
low, drier air filters in across the Florida peninsula from the 
north, with rain chances falling below 10% areawide. It is 
important to note that changes in rainfall timing cannot be ruled 
out given the discrepancies between guidance.

Temperatures through mid to late week are forecast to generally 
be near-normal and seasonable during the afternoon hours and near 
to slightly above normal through the overnight hours. A slight 
cooling trend looks to occur behind the passage of the low 
pressure, especially across northern portions of east central 
Florida.
